This vessel is central to making wave energy cost-effective and scalable. The Role As Shipbuild Project Manager, you will be the owner’s representative throughout the newbuild project, from shipyard selection to delivery and the warranty period. You will make sure the vessel is delivered on time, within budget, to the agreed quality, and fit for its mission of handling WECs safely and efficiently. You will work closely with our engineering, operations and finance teams as well as external partners. Alongside the newbuild, you will help build the organisation that will crew, operate, maintain and manage the vessel. For the right candidate, the role offers a natural path into a Vessel Manager role once the vessel is delivered. Key Responsibilities Shipyard selection and contracting Prepare tender documentation together with the ship designer and internal stakeholders. Identify, pre-qualify and evaluate shipyards on technical capability, capacity, financial strength, track record and price. Lead or support negotiations of the shipbuilding contract, specification, payment terms, guarantees, and delivery schedule. Project execution and follow-up Follow up the shipbuilding contract, including milestones, payments, variation orders, and claims. Follow up the ship designer, including design progress, drawing approval and design changes Manage interfaces between yard, designer, equipment suppliers, and our WEC engineering team, so the vessel and the WEC handling concept work together. Follow up the classification and flag state approval process, including plan approval, surveys, and certification. Follow up the design, integration and approval of systems for remote and/or unmanned operation, including the interface between the vessel and the remote operations centre. Site supervision and quality Carry out regular shipyard site visits, and lead or coordinate an owner’s site team during construction. Follow up quality assurance, inspections, testing, HSE performance and non-conformities. Attend and follow up FAT, harbour acceptance tests, sea trials, commissioning, and delivery. Budget, schedule and risk Ensure the project stays within budget and timeline through active cost control, forecasting, and schedule management. Identify, assess, and mitigate project risks. Report status, risks and key decisions to management. Preparing for operations Support the setup of the organisation and structure for crewing, operating, maintaining and managing the vessel. Contribute to setting up safety management systems, maintenance systems, spare parts strategy and technical documentation. After delivery Follow up guarantee claims during the warranty period. Lead or support the transition from project to operations. Required Experience and competence : MSc or BSc in naval architecture, marine engineering, mechanical engineering or similar At least 8 years of experience in shipbuilding or offshore projects, including at least one complete newbuild project from contract to delivery. Experience representing the owner (or working on the yard side) in newbuild projects, including site supervision. Solid understanding of shipbuilding contracts, specifications, and variation order management Experience with classification societies and flag state approval processes, and working knowledge of relevant IMO regulations. Proven track record of managing budgets, schedules, and suppliers in complex projects. Fluent English, spoken and written. Strong negotiation skills. Willing to travel, including periods at the shipyard. Desirable Experience with specialised vessels such as construction vessels, anchor handlers, multicats or workboats. Experience with dynamic positioning (DP) systems, deck handling equipment, and mission equipment integration. Experience with remotely operated or unmanned surface vessels (USVs), including remote operations centres, autonomy or remote-control systems, and the associated class and regulatory approval processes. Background from offshore renewables (wind, wave, tidal) or oil and gas. As a Person You are striving for excellence, put quality into everything you do You are self-motivated and constantly seek the most efficient ways to work You always search for simple and elegant solutions to difficult problems You love to learn new things, and take pride in constantly developing your skills You are persistent, knowing it takes stamina to reach pioneering goals You see your tasks through to completion You are comfortable in presenting your solutions internally and externally You are data driven and strive to always back your points with solid analysis CorPower Ocean has a highly diversified team with many nationalities and backgrounds, all working towards the same goal. This is something we are very proud of.

review_candidates.title: Senior Research Assistant (OA bipolar group)
review_candidates.company: Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
review_candidates.description: Older adults with bipolar disorder experience a range of complex and often under-recognised needs, including cognitive difficulties, physical and mental health comorbidities, reduced social support and difficulties with psychosocial functioning. This research project aims to address this gap by co-producing a group-based psychosocial intervention for older adults with bipolar and their carers. The research is funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Research Programme for Social Care (RPSC). It is a collaboration between Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust and the University of Manchester. The project’s Lead Investigators are Dr Elizabeth Tyler and Professor Steven Jones. The post holder will be based with the Research and Innovation Department at Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust, which hosts a number of large mental health trials and other research studies. The post holder will also have close links with the University of Manchester, School of Health Sciences where the Lead Investigator is based. We strive to be an inclusive research unit, and we welcome applicants from a diverse range of communities to apply for the post, including people from diverse ethnic communities, people who identify as LGBTQIA+, and/or who identify as having a disability or as being neurodivergent. The Post Holder Will Be Expected To Have Proven And Substantial Experience In Conducting Research; For Example, By Having Previously Assisted In The Running Of a Funded Research Study And/or a Postgraduate (Masters Or PhD) Study. The Post-holder Will Contribute To a Four-stage Programme Of Research Systematic review: Lead a systematic review of existing psychosocial interventions for people with bipolar, their carers, and older adults with bipolar disorder, to inform intervention development. Qualitative interviews: Lead participant recruitment and conducting qualitative interviews with older adults with bipolar and carers to explore their experiences, needs and preferences. The postholder will contribute to the qualitative analysis of interview data. Co-production: Supporting the facilitation of co-production groups involving older adults with bipolar, carers and professionals to develop and refine the intervention. The postholder will contribute to the qualitative analysis of co-production data and its integration into intervention development. Intervention refinement: Contributing to the final review and refinement of the intervention, ensuring that the perspectives of people with lived experience, carers and professionals are incorporated. The postholder will contribute to participant recruitment, systematic review activities, qualitative data collection and analysis, co-production sessions, intervention development and dissemination of research findings. Greater Manchester Mental Health (GMMH) Foundation Trust employs over 7000 members of staff, who deliver services from more than 122 locations. We provide inpatient and community-based mental health care for people living in Bolton, the city of Manchester, Salford, Trafford and the borough of Wigan, and a wide range of specialist mental health and substance misuse services across Greater Manchester, the north west of England and beyond. Greater Manchester is one of the world's most innovative, original and exciting places to live and work. From the beauty of the surrounding countryside to the heart of the vibrant inner city with great shopping, entertainment and dining options. Wherever you go you will experience a great northern welcome with people famed for their warmth, humour and generosity. Our people enjoy their work, have opportunities to learn and develop their skills and are encouraged to generate new ideas that improve care for our service users. For further details / informal visits contact: Name: Elizabeth Tyler Job title: Clinical Lecturer Email address: elizabeth.tyler@manchester.ac.uk
